rfp_requirements.title: Provide Access-Controlled Webpage for ERT Repair Data Entry
rfp_requirements.description: Provide an access-controlled webpage to allow authorized ERTs to enter repair data.

rfp_requirements.title: Develop ERT Repair Data Entry Module in Management Console
rfp_requirements.description: Contractor must develop and maintain a limited access repair data entry module within the Management Console for ERTs.

rfp_requirements.title: Motorist Hotline Availability and Response Standards
rfp_requirements.description: The Motorist Hotline shall be available to the public during principal operating hours, and 98% of calls must be received and placed in a call queue, answered within 10 minutes from the queue, or receive a return call to the motorist within 2 Motorist Hotline Business Hours.

rfp_requirements.title: Take over existing toll-free hotline number
rfp_requirements.description: The existing toll-free number shall be taken over by the successful Contractor upon commencement of its CIF operation, and revert to State upon contract termination.

rfp_requirements.title: Hire and train all Call Center Representatives
rfp_requirements.description: Contractor shall hire and train all CCRs.

rfp_requirements.title: Secure advance written SCM approval for motorist appointment system
rfp_requirements.description: Obtain advance, written SCM approval for use or implementation of any motorist appointment system.

rfp_requirements.title: Make reservation system accessible via website and telephone
rfp_requirements.description: Reservation system must be accessible to customers via the Contractor's website and by telephone.

Subject: Solicitation 3522R12, Emissions Program Management
Dear Ms. Grabuloff,
Parsons Transportation Group Inc. (Parsons) is pleased to provide this proposal to the Pennsylvania Department of
Transportation (PennDOT), Bureau of Office Services, in response to Request for Proposal (RFP) Number 3522R12
for Emissions Program Management.
Our commitment to PennDOT is to continue delivering an effective Pennsylvania Vehicle Emissions Inspection and
Maintenance Program and to innovate responsibly to move the Program forward. Building on our past performance,
we will implement new, cloud-based VIID systems and improved auditing infrastructure that efficiently gets Program
data to PennDOT. Our upgrades to the e-SAFETY system will support the enhanced safety inspection Program
compliance. We will upgrade our call center solution with new technology using ZenDesk and AmazonConnect as
the backbone of the system.
Our Program Mana

auditor teams, support teams, and subcontractors are in place. In this challenging
labor market, we do not anticipate any staffing impacts as your selected vendor in the new contract. Upon Notice to
Proceed, with no transitional risk to current operations, we will begin the implementation tasks to fulfill all RFP
requirements.
Parsons continues its commitment to Small Diverse Businesses and Small Businesses for this procurement.
Additionally, we have added two Veteran Business Enterprises to our team, 1Alpha Consulting to bolster our
motorist compliance activities and Berry Solutions Group for our information and education development and to
provide enhanced auditor training.
Offeror Responsibilities and Exceptions to the RFP Requirements
All information submitted pertains exclusively to Parsons Transportation Group Inc. as a subsidiary of Parsons
Corporation. Our proposal satisfies all mandatory requirements listed in the RFP, and we take no exceptions to any
of the contractual provisions outlined in the RFP.

I-5D: Program Changes
We recognize that PennDOT reserves the right to renegotiate the contract terms in the event of needed changes
prompted by legislative (federal or state) requirements, compliance with legally binding cou

e with PennDOT, providing updates and information until the emergency conditions
are mitigated or operations return to normal. Parsons’ PA I/M Management operations has built-in redundancy with three
regional offices located in Pittsburgh, Harrisburg, and Philadelphia that contain similar management and staff positions,
communications, and data transfer capabilities. As proven during the COVID-19 pandemic, our entire project team,
including management, office, call center, and field staff, are equipped to work remotely, enabling continuation of critical
business services without facility access.
If a particular region is affected by an emergency, operations can be directed to any of the remaining operational regions.
All management, office, and quality assurance personnel can support operations in other regions and continue providing
essential business activities. Quality assurance personnel can be productive in any area of the state, allowing for
coverage if some staff members are unavailable due to emergency conditions.
Similarly, if one or more regional offices closes due to emergencies such as a natural or man-made disaster, loss of
power/communications/network connectivity, qu

y, quarantine, or pandemic control measures, all essential business activities
will be redirected to remaining operational regional offices and to project staff working remotely. For example, Parsons
will forward telephone numbers to unaffected regional offices to ensure station and consumer issues are addressed. All
regional Program information is stored remotely, preventing loss and allowing access by other regional and remote
project staff during unplanned office closures.
If an emergency impacts a VIID hosting location or VIID functionality, the Disaster Recovery Plan (referenced in I-5G
above and Attachment B) will be implemented to minimize or avoid disruption of critical business functions.
If an emergency impacts the stations’ ability to connect to the VIID, our systems will be able to continue testing for 30
days or 100 inspections, as per the offline test limits set by the VIID and determined by PennDOT. Allowing offline testing
minimizes negative impacts to both the inspection industry and the public. Once connectivity is restored, any offline
testing will automatically upload to the VIID.
Customer service and station operator hotlines are also covered in our emergency p

tted to controlling the
system, troubleshooting any problems that may arise, and making changes as needed to resolve system issues.
A.6 Maintenance of Database Access for Emission Inspection Stations
We will modernize the web portal application using new technologies available in the AWS cloud environment to
develop mobile-friendly features with the web portal for use on a mobile device. In addition, the web portal application
will allow us to perform maintenance tasks for:
§ Adding and deleting technician access numbers and access codes
§ Setting and clearing lockouts
§ Sending messages to the inspection stations per instructions from PennDOT
We will work with all approved equipment manufacturers to ensure that software updates can be transmitted to the
inspection units capable of receiving them. We will ensure that this process is closely controlled and monitored to
maintain the highest level of program integrity. We will troubleshoot any reported problems and make changes to the
appropriate tables as required to ensure stations and inspectors can perform inspection tasks as required and
